explanation: Compared against Written on the Wall II (archived all.html, snapshot of 26 July 2026, and the definitions file wowIIdefs.js from cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/, via the Wayback Machine; the live site does not respond), Conjecture 291: 'If G is a simple connected graph such that n(G) > 2, then γ_t(G) ≤ k + frequency t_min(v), where k is the first step in which a zero appears in the Havil-Hakimi process', with the note 'Mar. 1, 2007, July 23, 2026 Zyad Tamimi, sent a 12-vertex counterexample, γ_t(G) = 4, frequency t_min(v) = 1 and k = 2.' The Lean declaration is the negation of the universal statement (finite type with more than two vertices, connected G) totalDominationNumber G ≤ havelHakimiZeroStep G + freqMinTriangles G. totalDominationNumber is the least size of a set D such that every vertex has a neighbour in D; freqMinTriangles is the number of vertices attaining the minimum number of incident triangles (WOWII definition 51); havelHakimiZeroStep is the least number i of Havel–Hakimi steps after which the sequence contains a zero (or is empty). I checked the 12-vertex graph G_6 from upstream issue #4562 (book graph with six triangular pages on spine ab, plus p ~ x_1, b; q ~ x_1, a, ℓ; r ~ x_2, x_3 with x_2 ~ x_3; leaf ℓ): degree sequence 8,8,4,4,4,3,2,2,2,2,2,1; after one step 7,3,3,3,2,2,2,1,1,1,1 (no zero), after two steps a zero appears, so k = 2 in the Lean indexing, the same value the source records; ℓ is the only vertex in no triangle, so the frequency is 1; and γ_t = 4 (q is forced by the leaf, N(p) and N(r) are disjoint, and x_4 forces a or b). So 4 ≤ 3 fails and the negated statement is the correct resolution, with the step indexing agreeing with the source's own bookkeeping. Faithful. Minor: the question tag is used although the source states a conjecture.
